manifest.title: Skill sync
manifest.intro: The manifest records only how each skill was installed (repository, path, version) and never uploads skill files. When you are signed in to GitHub it is uploaded with your memories; without signing in you can export a manifest file and import it on another computer.
manifest.noRemoteLoggedOut: Not signed in to GitHub, so the cloud manifest is unavailable. Sign in and sync once, or import a manifest file exported on another computer.
manifest.noRemoteLoggedIn: There is no manifest in the cloud yet. Sync once and your other computers will see this computer's skills.
manifest.onlyHereNote: They are added to the manifest the next time you upload to the cloud.
manifest.localOnlyCount: {n} of them have no source address; only the name is recorded and they must be copied by hand
manifest.installBody: Each one is downloaded from its repository and installed here. Existing folders with the same name are not overwritten.

prompt.title: Extraction prompt
prompt.desc: The rules sent to the model on every extraction. Rewrite them to suit you, for example to record only certain kinds of things.
prompt.hint: Use {placeholder} for the project name; it is filled in when the prompt runs.
prompt.emptyHint: Saving it empty uses the built-in prompt.
prompt.appended: These keep extraction safe and let MemDock read the result, so they always follow your rules. After them come the current memory files, the conversation excerpt and the required output format.

quota.explain: Shows how much of your 5-hour and weekly Claude Code quota is left on the usage page. Uses your existing Claude Code sign-in; no extra login, and your account details are never stored. Updates every 30 minutes, or refresh it yourself on the usage page.

quota.codexExplain: Shows how much of your 5-hour and weekly Codex quota is left on the usage page. Uses your existing ChatGPT sign-in in Codex; no extra login, and your account details are never stored. Updates every 30 minutes, or refresh it yourself on the usage page. When off, the quota recorded the last time you used Codex is shown.
